headline: High: shared filesystem/RAG and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; no direct isolation evidence for the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and supports retrieval-based chat. That creates a plausible path where content from one agent is ingested by the other as trusted text. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Haystack ingests Khoj-produced text through MCP or REST without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF Khoj indexes Haystack outputs as notes or documents, attacker-controlled instructions can persist into retrieval.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of agent outputs into retrieval indexes.
Add provenance labels and strip instructions before indexing.
Require human review for any retrieved content that triggers tool use.
Restrict MCP endpoints to allowlisted schemas only.
requires-engineering: add content-safety filters at the ingestion boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files plus model-provider API keys for self-hosted use. If either agent processes the other's sensitive workspace content, data can leave the local boundary through outbound API calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Haystack sends retrieved notes to external APIs, personal notes may be exposed.
IF Khoj indexes files containing secrets and Haystack queries them, those secrets can be forwarded in prompts or logs.
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces.
Block outbound traffic except to approved endpoints.
Exclude secret-bearing directories from Khoj indexing.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack exposes REST/MCP calls and broad egress, while Khoj has read-only filesystem access and no write_filesystem or modify_git_state. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource contention is limited. The main conflict is operational rather than destructive, keeping severity low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external API quota, they can contend for rate limits.
IF an orchestrator maps both to the same shared network credential, requests may interfere.
mitigations: Assign separate API keys per agent.
Set per-agent rate limits.
Avoid sharing mutable git or filesystem targets.
Monitor 429/error spikes during concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system and Khoj is a retrieval-based conversational agent, so one agent's output can plausibly become the other's input. If Khoj treats Haystack-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream answers or actions. No verification step is documented in the pair, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Khoj consumes Haystack summaries without source verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF Haystack retrieves stale or incorrect documents that Khoj then cites, downstream outputs inherit the error.
mitigations: Require source links for every retrieved claim.
Add a verification pass before any action-taking.
Mark generated summaries as untrusted until checked.
Limit Khoj to read-only responses for Haystack-fed content.
requires-engineering: implement citation-grounded validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents and may use cloud or self-hosted servers, while Haystack touches anonymous usage statistics and broad network egress. If personal notes include regulated data, the pair can create retention or residency mismatches, but the profiles do not prove a specific regulated class or jurisdiction, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF personal notes contain regulated data and Khoj forwards them to a cloud provider, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF Haystack logs retrieved content beyond anonymous usage statistics, retention controls may diverge from Khoj's policies.
mitigations: Classify data before indexing.
Keep regulated notes out of cloud-backed flows.
Review retention settings for both agents.
Document the hosting region for each API endpoint.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention.
